findings.title: Stopped-agent count includes agents whose stop call failed
findings.description: `_stop_background` catches a failed `stop_task` per id and continues, but then sets `self.background_tasks_stopped = len(ids)` unconditionally. The count is written into step metadata as `background_tasks_stopped`, and the warning at line 345 lists every id as "stopped". If one of two stops fails, the metadata reports 2. The test `test_stop_task_failure_is_logged_and_next_id_still_stopped` in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py` checks the logged error and the call order, but never asserts the count. Track successes separately and assert the count in that test.

findings.title: `set_model` bypasses the unusable-session guard
findings.description: `unusable_reason` is documented at lines 125–126 as "every later call then raises". `dispatch`, `compact`, and `seed_context` call `_require_usable()`, but `set_model` does not. After a failed rotation, `_reconnect` resets `current_model` to `None`, so the next session step calls `set_model` on the never-connected client (`dispatch.py:353`) before `dispatch()` raises the "SDK session unusable" message. What the SDK raises from an unconnected client is unverified here. The test suite cannot show the difference, because the fresh client's `set_model` is an `AsyncMock` in `tests/pipeline/conftest.py`. Add the guard to `set_model`, and give the fake client a `set_model` that fails when not connected.

findings.title: Synchronous config-file reads run on the event loop
findings.description: `_background_idle_timeout_s` is called from the async `_collect_turns` (line 224). `open_pipeline_session` (lines 458–460) and `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` (`dispatch.py:147,153`) are also async and call `get_typed_config`. Each call runs `load_config`, which does two synchronous `open()` and `tomllib` reads (`config/manager.py:82–102`). The project rule requires that synchronous code in async functions be guaranteed under 1 ms, and file reads cannot guarantee that. The same pattern predates this diff (`openai/provider.py:63`, `tools/cf_tools.py:221`), but the new call sites add to it. Read the config once in `open_pipeline_session`, store the value on the session, and reuse it. Use `asyncio.to_thread` for any remaining reads.

findings.title: Step-metadata key contract is written twice
findings.description: `describe_run_settings` in `core/models.py:125–131` builds `system_prompt_mode`, `setting_sources`, and `auto_memory`. The session path of `DispatchAction` builds the same three keys by hand (`dispatch.py:371–375`). A rename or a change to one copy silently breaks the other. Have the session path call a shared helper that takes the session's values, or move the key construction into one function.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` is 473 lines and holds too many responsibilities
findings.description: The project guideline is about 300 lines per source file. The class now owns rotation, the turn-read loop, rate-limit retry, the idle timer, background-agent stopping, and the settings builder. The read loop (`_collect_turns`, `_read_turn_with_retry`, `_read_turn`, `_stop_background`, roughly lines 215–349) depends only on the client and the turn ledger. Move it to a module that takes the client as a parameter, next to `sdk_turns.py`.

findings.title: Blanket `except Exception` that does not re-raise
findings.description: `_stop_background` catches `Exception` with `# noqa: BLE001`, logs with `logger.exception`, and continues. Project rule (a) requires re-raising after the log, and rule (b) requires a specific exception type. The comment gives a reason, but the rule does not allow a blanket catch in this position. The failure is logged but its outcome is not recorded (see the count finding above). Either record failures and surface them in the dispatch result, or catch the narrowest type the SDK actually raises.

findings.title: Zero or negative idle timeout is accepted and stops agents immediately
findings.description: `_coerce_value` (`config/manager.py:75–76`) does a bare `int(raw_value)`, and `get_typed_config` checks only the type. `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s = 0` therefore stores and reads back. `asyncio.timeout(0)` expires at once, so every waiting dispatch stops its background agents immediately. A user who reads 0 as "disabled" gets that behavior. Validate at the config boundary: reject values below 1, or define an explicit disable value and document it in the key description.

findings.title: No load test for the new concurrency path
findings.description: The project's Python rules require at least one `tests/load/` test for code on concurrency or network paths, and assert latency or resource bounds there. This change adds an idle-timer read loop with stop and reconnect behavior, and no `tests/load/` file is in the diff. The slice's task review (`project-documents/user/reviews/932-review.tasks.pipeline-sdk-session-…md`, line 109) judged no load test necessary, but on NFR grounds, which is narrower than the rule. Either add a bounded-latency load test with a scripted client, or record an explicit exception against the rule.

findings.title: Idle expiry is detected by catching any builtin `TimeoutError`
findings.description: `_collect_turns` treats any builtin `TimeoutError` during a waiting read as idle silence, stops the agents, and returns a partial response with only a warning. If the SDK raises its own `TimeoutError` during that read, it is misclassified. Whether the SDK does so is unverified. Checking the timeout context's own `expired()` state would remove the ambiguity.

findings.title: Test helpers are typed `object` and hidden behind `type: ignore`
findings.description: `_ledger_after(...) -> object` forces `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` at each use. `scripted_session` and `failing_reconnect_patch` in `tests/pipeline/conftest.py` have the same `-> object` return. `failing_reconnect_patch` is then used as a context manager. Pyright does not check tests (`pyproject.toml` sets `include = ["src"]`), so this is not a merge blocker. Return the concrete types.

findings.title: Settings policy docstring contradicts the documented `sq serve` exception
findings.description: The module docstring says "no automated path may leave `setting_sources` unset". `provider.py:89–90` and `core/models.py:110` document `sq serve` as passing `None`, which loads the CLI default. Either scope the docstring to pipeline and review paths, or name the exception in it.

findings.title: `SystemPromptMode` docstring points at a table in another class
findings.description: "The four rows of the table above" refers to the table in `AgentConfig` at lines 49–58, which is not directly above this enum. That table labels the `(False, None)` row "(none)", while the enum calls the same case `EMPTY`. Point the docstring at the table by name, and align the two labels.

findings.title: Mode derivation duplicates the provider's branching
findings.description: `describe_system_prompt` repeats the truth table in `providers/sdk/provider.py:58–64`. The two agree today, and the models test checks only the table. Nothing links the recorded mode to what the provider actually sends. Have the provider compute the mode, or add a test that drives `create_agent` and compares its output with `describe_system_prompt`.

findings.title: `pyright: ignore` covers a settings type mismatch
findings.description: `settings["setting_sources"]` is a `list[str]`, and the `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` suppresses the mismatch with the SDK's options type. If the SDK types `setting_sources` as a `Literal` list (unverified here), type the settings module with that alias and drop the suppression.
